ratings.rationale: Unauthenticated ADS-B content permits fabricated tracks; LEO reception alone does not authenticate. Cross-check/MLAT may expose inconsistency at L3. Evidence supports ADS-B spoofing generally.
ratings.issue: Acts on A1.1 but attacker emitter is not a registered asset; cross-check limits deception.

ratings.rationale: Replay spoofs stale/displaced ADS-B content; MLAT localization and cross-check can detect position/time inconsistency. Evidence is terrestrial ADS-B, so analogue downgrade.
ratings.issue: Replay may be exposed by MLAT position/time consistency; evidence is terrestrial, not LEO MLAT.

ratings.rationale: Aircraft-origin false position is spoofing of the self-report; E-MLAT/ADS-B cross-check is the designed detector. Documented incidents support evidence but are not LEO MLAT.
ratings.issue: Only cross-check can detect; successful masking is integrity deception, not displacement.

ratings.rationale: In-band jamming raises noise floor and denies reception over a footprint. Detection is expected at RF/front-end level. Evidence is terrestrial ADS-B, so analogue downgrade.
ratings.issue: Jamming is denial, not spoofing; footprint-wide scope is assumed.

ratings.rationale: Synchronised emitters can synthesize consistent TDOA for a ghost target; AOA may separate them depending on geometry. Evidence is terrestrial multilateration, so analogue downgrade.
ratings.issue: Overlaps ghost-target concept; detectability depends on AOA geometry and pass.

ratings.rationale: Synchronised emitters overshadowing a real aircraft can displace a genuine track; goal is displacement. Evidence is terrestrial multilateration; LEO feasibility remains uncertain.
ratings.issue: Distinct from T1.05 by displacement goal; multi-emitter feasibility in LEO unproven.

ratings.rationale: Targeted suppression denies chosen aircraft while leaving others; impact is local denial. Detection at RF/reception level. Evidence is analogue to terrestrial/aviation systems.
ratings.issue: Selective nulling against LEO payload not evidenced; denial scope narrow.

ratings.rationale: High-rate 1090 MHz traffic can saturate payload decode chain, causing footprint denial. Evidence is LEO-network DoS, not 1090 MHz payload flooding; analogue downgrade.
ratings.issue: Evidence is LEO-network DoS, not 1090 MHz payload flooding.

ratings.rationale: Biasing TOA/FOA/AOA modifies genuine observables before stamping, causing position error with nominal integrity. Strong pass may detect large single-satellite bias; weak pass has stealth window.
ratings.issue: TOA/FOA/AOA bias overlaps timing and RF spoofing; evidence not from LEO MLAT.

ratings.rationale: GNSS jamming denies the disciplining input, forcing holdover and degrading timing quality; later drift can bias observables. Detection is at GNSS receiver/L1. Evidence is aviation analogue.
ratings.issue: Immediate effect is input loss; drift consequence depends on holdover, so partly enabler.

ratings.rationale: Counterfeit GNSS pulls the GNSS-disciplined clock, biasing every stamped observable while reports remain authentic. Strong pass detects large single-satellite bias; weak pass has stealth window.
ratings.issue: Assumes covert 100 ns step escapes L1 checks; satellite GNSS spoofing not directly evidenced.

ratings.rationale: Weak command authentication enables unauthorised bus/payload control but has no direct target-report consequence. It is an enabler for timing or observable manipulation.
ratings.issue: Enabler only; hosted-asset edges inferred and not fully supported.

ratings.rationale: Memory-safety exploitation can yield platform control, but by itself does not alter a target report. It is an enabler for later payload/clock compromise.
ratings.issue: Enabler; no direct target-report consequence until chained.

ratings.rationale: Firmware alteration or secure-boot bypass gives persistent platform control but no direct target-report effect. It enables later manipulation. Starlink terminal evidence is analogue.
ratings.issue: Enabler; Starlink terminal evidence is analogue; update path not LEO-MLAT specific.

ratings.rationale: Remote terminal compromise can disrupt ground-station reception or command path, causing denial. Evidence is SATCOM-terminal analogue. Detection likely at L2 management/log level.
ratings.issue: SATCOM terminal evidence is analogue; ground-station scope may overlap L2.

ratings.rationale: RF interference or resource exhaustion at a ground station blocks downlink/telecommand, causing regional denial. Evidence is LEO-network DoS analogue; detection at ground-station level.
ratings.issue: RF and resource-exhaustion mechanisms are conflated; evidence is LEO-network DoS.

rubric_ambiguities: Di_strong/Di_weak are undefined for non-timing threats; I used judgement or same value.
Damage for enablers with denial effects is unclear; I followed D null for enablers.
Analogue_only interpretation for terrestrial ADS-B/GNSS evidence against LEO MLAT is ambiguous.
A extent for satellite footprint versus aircraft count is uncertain.
Distinguishing T1.05 ghost and T1.06 takeover depends on intent.
batch_comments.overall: The batch covers L1 well but is thin on L2-L4. Many enablers and analogue evidence reduce confidence. T1.08 and T1.16 conflate mechanisms; T1.05/T1.06 overlap. Timing threats depend heavily on assumptions W1-W3.
